questions.question: Has any applicant been involved in a loan default, settlement, or acted as guarantor on an unpaid loan?
questions.description:
🛡️ Credit History Check
This helps lenders assess creditworthiness. A history of defaults, settlements, or acting as guarantor on defaulted loans may affect lender eligibility.
💡 Tip: Being honest helps find the right lenders who can work with the applicant's credit history.

options.label: Yes — involved in default or settlement
Yes — was guarantor on unpaid/settled loan

condition.then: A prior loan default or settlement where applicant acted as a guarantor may also affect lender eligibility. If no offers appear, applicant may explore our DSA pool, where a few DSAs may assist subject to additional fees or risk mitigation, such as collateral.

questions.question: Which type of area is this plot located in?

The surrounding area helps determine which lenders can finance the property.
💡 Tip: Choose the option that best matches how the area looks and is commonly described.

options.label: Planned / Development Authority Area
options.helperText: approved layout, township, large housing society

options.label: Converted Land / Approved Residential Use
options.helperText: earlier agricultural or village land, now residential

options.helperText: inside city limits, older houses, narrow streets

options.label: Not sure
options.helperText: I'm not certain about the area classification

questions.question: Does the property fall under any special restricted zone?
questions.description:
⛔ Special Restricted Zone
Some zones have additional restrictions that affect which lenders can process the application.

options.label: Cantonment Board area
options.helperText: Military/defense area with special building rules

condition.then: Properties in tribal/Schedule V areas have severe transfer restrictions. Most banks will not finance. Specialized NBFCs may consider at higher rates.
Coastal Regulation Zone properties face construction restrictions. Only CRZ-II (developed urban coastal) is generally financeable with proper environmental clearances.
Cantonment Board properties require additional clearances from the Board. Most banks accept but processing takes longer.
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) is not applicable in this state. Please verify the property location is actually in a coastal state.
Cantonment Board areas are not present in this state. Please verify the property location.

questions.question: What is the land use classification of this plot?
questions.description:
🏗️ Land Use Classification
Land classification determines whether the plot is financeable. Agricultural land CANNOT be financed through standard bank loans — NA conversion must be completed first.
💡 Tip: Check the 7/12 extract, Patta, or revenue records for the official land classification. If converted, keep the NA Sanad/order ready.

condition.then: Agricultural land cannot be financed through standard bank loans. NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion must be completed first. If conversion is in progress, the loan can only be processed after the NA Sanad/order is obtained.

Industrial plot financing is handled as a project/business loan by most lenders. Standard plot loan products may not be available. Consider applying under Business Loan if this is for commercial/industrial use.

questions.question: How was this plot originally acquired / from whom?
questions.description:
📋 Plot Source
The source of the plot is the #1 eligibility filter for plot loans. Authority allotments get near-universal acceptance, while revenue sites are refused by most banks.

options.label: Development Authority allotment (DDA, HUDA, BDA, etc.)

condition.then: Revenue layout plots are formed without planning authority approval. Most nationalised banks refuse to finance revenue sites. Processing will proceed but lender options may be severely limited. Only select NBFCs may consider this.

questions.question: Which development authority allotted this plot?
questions.description: Select the government development authority that originally allotted this plot.

The type of ownership determines your rights over the property and affects loan eligibility.
FreeholdFull ownership rights forever
LeaseholdRights for a specific period
📌 Key Points:
  • Freehold properties are preferred by most lenders
  • Leasehold requires checking remaining lease period
  • Some lenders may need lease extension proof
questions.question: Please indicate the type of ownership for the property?
How many years are remaining on the lease?

condition.then: Leasehold properties with less than 20 years remaining are extremely difficult to finance. Most banks will reject.

questions.question: When was this plot first allotted or sold?
questions.description: Select the approximate age since the plot was first allotted by authority or first sold. This helps determine title chain requirements.

condition.then: Area should not be greater than 10,00,000

questions.question: What is the boundary demarcation status of this plot?
questions.description: Banks require clear boundary demarcation for physical verification and valuation. Unclear boundaries can delay or prevent loan approval.

condition.then: Banks require clear boundary demarcation for physical verification. This may delay or prevent loan approval. Consider getting a boundary survey done before applying.

questions.question: What type of construction is planned / being built?
questions.description: Select the type of building being constructed on this plot. This affects loan terms, LTV ratio, and documentation requirements.

questions.description: Approved building plans are required by lenders before construction disbursement begins.

condition.then: Most lenders require an approved building plan before sanctioning the construction component. The plot purchase portion may still proceed, but construction disbursement will be held until plan approval.

questions.question: Has the building received its OC (Occupancy Certificate) / CC (Completion Certificate)?
questions.description: OC/CC is proof that the construction complies with approved building plans. Required for completed buildings.

questions.question: Was the building plan approved / sanctioned by the local municipal authority?
questions.description: Municipal approval (building permission) is required for all new construction.

questions.question: Who is handling the construction?
questions.description: The type of constructor affects documentation requirements and disbursement process.

questions.question: What is the current status of construction on this plot?
questions.description: For balance transfer of composite loans, the current construction status determines documentation and valuation requirements.

questions.question: Is this plot in an approved layout with development authority / municipal corporation approval?
questions.description:
🏛️ Plot Compliance — Development Authority Area
Plots in approved layouts by development authorities (DDA, HUDA, BDA, etc.) have the highest lender acceptance. Allotment letter + possession letter is usually sufficient documentation.

options.label: Yes — approved layout, all permissions in place
Approved area but some permissions pending
Not in an approved / authorized layout

condition.then: Plots not in an approved layout face significantly limited financing options. Only select NBFCs may consider this. Proceed with caution.

questions.question: Has this plot been fully converted from agricultural to non-agricultural (NA) use with valid conversion order?
questions.description:
⚠️ Plot Compliance — Converted Land
NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion is mandatory for bank financing. Without a valid NA Sanad/order, no bank or NBFC will process this loan.
💡 Tip: Keep the NA conversion order / Sanad ready. State-specific: Maharashtra (NA order from Collector), Karnataka (DC conversion), Gujarat (NA Sanad from Mamlatdar).

options.label: Yes — fully converted with NA Sanad/order

condition.then: NA conversion is still pending. Loan processing can begin but disbursement will be held until the conversion order is obtained. Keep the application reference number ready.
Unconverted agricultural land CANNOT be financed through standard bank loans. NA conversion must be completed before any lender will process this application.

questions.question: Is this plot within municipal corporation limits with proper layout approval and building permission zone?
questions.description:
🏛️ Plot Compliance — Municipal Area
Plots within municipal limits with proper zoning and layout approval have good lender acceptance. Municipal property records and tax receipts are key documents.

options.label: Yes — within municipal limits, proper layout approval
Within municipal limits but layout approval unclear
Outside municipal limits / no proper approval

condition.then: Plots outside municipal limits or without proper layout approval face limited financing options. Only select NBFCs may consider this.

questions.question: Is this colony / layout authorized by the development authority? Has the layout been approved?
questions.description:
⚠️ Plot Compliance — Colony / Village Area
Plots in unauthorized colonies or unapproved layouts are extremely difficult to finance. Regularization status is critical for lender acceptance.

condition.then: Plots in unauthorized colonies are rejected by virtually all lenders. Colony regularization must be completed or at least formally initiated before any bank will consider financing.

questions.question: Is the plot's legal status clear — does it have any form of government / municipal approval?
questions.description:
⚠️ Plot Compliance — Status Unknown
If the area type is unclear, the plot's legal and approval status becomes even more critical. Lenders will require clear documentation of the plot's authorization.

options.label: Yes — has some form of government approval

condition.then: Plots without any form of government approval are not financeable by standard lenders. Explore options to obtain at least basic municipal or panchayat approval before applying.

questions.question: What is the current status of the NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion order?
questions.description:
📜 NA Conversion Status
The NA order from the District Collector’s office is the key document proving land use has been changed from agricultural to residential.

options.label: Already in residential zone (no conversion needed)

condition.then: Without NA conversion, no lender can process this loan. The conversion process typically takes 2-6 months.

questions.question: What is the status of revenue records (7/12, Patta, Khata, RTC) for this plot?
questions.description: Revenue records are always required for plot loans — they confirm land ownership, classification, and mutation status. State-specific: 7/12 extract (MH/GJ), Patta/Chitta (TN), RTC (KA), Jamabandi (PB/HR/RJ).

options.label: Available and up to date
options.helperText: 7/12, Khata, Patta, RTC — whichever applies in your state

options.label: Available but not updated recently
options.helperText: Records exist but mutation or name transfer pending

condition.then: Properties without revenue records are extremely difficult to finance. Even specialized NBFCs require some form of ownership documentation.

questions.question: What type of layout approval does this plot have?
questions.description: Layout approval type determines the level of lender acceptance. Planning authority approved layouts get the best terms.

condition.then: Revenue layouts are not approved by planning authorities. Most banks refuse to finance plots in revenue layouts. Only select NBFCs may consider this.

questions.question: What is the zone classification of this land?
questions.description:
🗺️ Zone Classification
Zone classification determines permissible construction type. Lenders prefer residential or mixed-use zones.

condition.then: Commercial-zoned property: Some lenders may restrict residential loans on commercial-zoned land. Verify lender policy.

questions.question: Is the property / project RERA registered?
questions.description:
🏢 RERA Registration
RERA registration is mandatory for projects over 500 sq.m. Banks verify RERA number before sanctioning loans for under-construction properties.

condition.then: Banks will not finance under-construction projects without RERA registration. Verify with the builder.

questions.question: Is the property tax / land revenue tax being paid regularly for this plot?
questions.description:
💰 Municipal Tax Status
Regular tax payment history proves the property is recognized by the municipal body — an important signal for lenders.

options.label: Yes — paid regularly and up to date
Paid but with gaps or arrears

condition.then: Properties without municipal tax records are difficult to finance. Clearing arrears and obtaining tax receipts is recommended before applying.

questions.question: What is the road access to this plot?
questions.description: Road access is assessed during bank physical verification and affects plot valuation significantly.

condition.then: Plots without proper road access are extremely difficult to finance. Banks require access for physical verification and valuation. This may result in loan rejection by most lenders.

questions.question: What is the infrastructure development status of the area?
questions.description: Infrastructure availability (water, electricity, drainage, road) affects plot valuation and lender willingness.

questions.question: Are there any unauthorized structures or constructions on this plot?
questions.description: Even vacant plots may have temporary structures, boundary encroachments, or unauthorized constructions that affect valuation and legal status.

options.label: Minor additions (balcony enclosure, extra room)
options.helperText: Small changes that don't alter the building footprint significantly

condition.then: Major unauthorized construction significantly reduces lender options. Banks will likely reject; select NBFCs may consider at lower LTV and higher rates.

questions.question: Has this colony/layout been regularized by the government?
questions.description:
🏘️ Colony Regularization
Many villages and panchayat areas have colonies that were developed informally but later regularized by state government orders. Regularized colonies are accepted by more lenders.

questions.question: Has the Gram Panchayat issued permission for this construction?
questions.description:
🏡 Gram Panchayat Permission
In panchayat areas, the Gram Panchayat is the local authority that grants building permission. This serves as proof of authorized construction.

questions.question: How did the current owner(s) acquire this property?
questions.description:
📜 Acquisition Method
GPA (Power of Attorney) transfers are rejected by most lenders after the Supreme Court ruling. Inherited properties need succession documents.

condition.then: GPA transfers are not legally valid sales (Supreme Court ruling). Most lenders will reject. Only specialized HFCs may consider at very high rates.
Inherited properties need succession certificate / legal heir certificate / probate. All legal heirs must be co-applicants or provide NOC.

questions.question: Is this property inherited? If so, is the succession properly documented?
questions.description:
🏠 Succession Status
For inherited properties, lenders require succession certificate, legal heir certificate, probate of will, or partition deed — depending on how the property was inherited.

options.label: Inherited — succession documents complete
options.helperText: Succession certificate, will probate, or mutation done

condition.then: Incomplete succession documentation will delay or prevent loan processing. Succession certificate or mutation must be completed first.

questions.question: Are the original property documents available?
questions.description: Lender holds original property documents as mortgage security. For plot loans, key originals include: sale deed/allotment letter, NA order (if converted), revenue records, encumbrance certificate, and approved layout plan.

condition.then: Original property documents are mandatory for mortgage creation. Without originals, no lender can process LAP.

questions.question: Is the ownership chain (title chain) complete and traceable?
questions.description:
🔗 Title Chain
Lenders need an unbroken chain of ownership from original allotment/sale to current owner.

questions.question: Is there any existing loan / mortgage on this property?

If property already has a loan, this becomes a Balance Transfer case.

options.label: No — property is free from any loan
Yes — existing mortgage on this property

questions.question: Is the property free from any legal disputes or litigation?

condition.then: Properties under active litigation are rejected by ALL lenders. Dispute must be resolved first.

questions.question: When do you plan to start construction on this plot?

questions.description:

Sometimes the actual deal value differs from what's declared in the Agreement to Sell (ATS) document.

📄 ATS/Sale Deed ValueRegistered amount
